title: late-binding-capacity-jitter-scratchpad
content:
Quick notes / running log (personal scratchpad) - investigating weird capacity jitter with late-binding pools and warmup churn.

TL;DR:
- Observed recurring capacity thrash on dedicated GPU late-binding pools between 2025-11-01 and 2025-11-03.
- Symptoms: sudden request queue growth -> scaler spins up nodes -> warmup latency spike -> requests rerouted -> downstream load oscillates.
- Hypotheses: (A) incorrect warm-start gating (cache warming vs readiness probe), (B) late-binding policy interaction with pooling TTL, (C) a race between health-check timeouts and prewarm token exchange.
- Repro steps + commands tried below, errors and snippets captured.

1) Incident snippets and observable metrics
- CPU/GPU allocation: spikes in GPU allocation for pool "lb-pool-8" at ~03:12 UTC and again at ~10:47 UTC.
- Requests queued metric (per-route): 0->180 in ~18s on heavy endpoints, average token latency doubled during warmups.
- Autoscaler logs show: "scaleUp requested=6 targetCapacity=12 reason=queued-backlog" then immediately another event: "scaleDown scheduled=2 reason=utilization-below-threshold" within 45s.
- Notable: many nodes reported readiness=true but runtime reported kv-cache-missing and then later recovered.

2) Commands / queries I executed (local / kubectl / monitoring)
- k get pods -n dedicated-lb --selector=pool=lb-pool-8 -o wide\  # checked pod ages and nodes
- kubectl logs pod/infra-autoscaler-0 -n infra -c autoscaler | grep "scaleUp requested" -A3 -B2
- curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?metric=requests_queued&pool=lb-pool-8&start=2025-11-01T02:00Z&end=2025-11-03T12:00Z" | jq '.'
- kubectl exec -it pod/model-runtime-xyz -c runtime -- sh -c "ls -la /kvcache || echo KV_MISSING"
- curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"route":"/nlp/generate","tokens":512}' https://staging.api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/debug/route-check
- ssh core@node-12 "journalctl -u model-runtime -n 200 --no-pager | grep -E 'warm|cache|kv'"

3) Raw error snips I captured
- autoscaler: WARN 2025-11-03T03:12:14Z scaler.go:244 scaleUp requested=6 err="insufficient warm nodes: 2/8 prewarm available"
- runtime: ERROR 2025-11-03T03:12:37Z runtime_cache.go:88 kvcache: miss for prefix key=chat-session-0x7b2f -> falling back to compute
- network: WARN 2025-11-03T03:13:02Z proxy.go:412 downstream timeout waiting for readiness probe: context deadline exceeded
- node: INFO 2025-11-03T03:13:05Z startup.go:132 runtime started, registered services, reported readiness=true
- autoscaler: DEBUG 2025-11-03T03:13:18Z decisions.go:76 considerScaleDown pool=lb-pool-8 idleSec=38 currentNodes=14 targetNodes=12

4) Timeline I stitched together (best-effort)
- 03:12:10 UTC: spike in queued requests (external load test + real traffic overlap).
- 03:12:14 UTC: autoscaler emits scaleUp requested because queued backlog > threshold. Requested +6 nodes.
- 03:12:37 UTC: new nodes begin runtime startup; kv-cache misses begin (warm cache not in place).
- 03:13:02 UTC: proxy sees some nodes as ready but runtime still loading model shards -> some readiness false positives -> proxy times out on a subset of connections.
- 03:13:18 UTC: autoscaler observes low utilization on a slice of the pool and schedules scaleDown for some nodes. Rapid decisions lead to net oscillation.

5) Immediate hypotheses - detail
- Hypothesis A (readiness gating mismatch): Our readiness probe is tied to process start + port open. It returns success before the model runtime has fully loaded KV caches and prefilled attention caches. As a result, proxy routes requests to nodes that will have high first-token latency, the autoscaler sees low sustained utilization and decides to scale more (because of queue), then scale down when initial bursts complete.
  - Evidence: runtime logs show "readiness=true" significantly earlier than "kvcache warm complete" messages.
  - Potential mitigation: change readiness probe to include a lightweight KV warm check or add a "serving-ready" endpoint that only flips after prewarm complete.

- Hypothesis B (late-binding policy + TTL): Late-binding pool schedules nodes lazily with short TTL for prewarmed instances. The autoscaler uses conservative thresholds to avoid overprovisioning, but TTLs are too short so nodes get recycled before subsequent bursts arrive, causing constant churn.
  - Evidence: node age histogram shows many nodes aged < 10m when churn occurs.
  - Potential mitigation: increase min-lifetime for prewarmed nodes or add burst-protection hold window.

- Hypothesis C (race in token exchange / KMS): Some nodes stall because they block on KMS token retrieval at startup (intermittent KMS throttling). This delays KV warming.
  - Evidence: a few node journal logs show "kms: request throttled, retrying" during startup.
  - Mitigation: add exponential backoff + background prefetch of tokens or allow serving to start without heavy KMS ops and lazy-load third-party secrets.

6) Experiments to run (quick cheap tests)
- A: Adjust readiness probe to check /internal/kv-health (simple boolean) on a canary pool and run synthetic load to see if proxy avoids early routing.
- B: Increase prewarm TTL to 20m on lb-pool-8 for a 2-hour window and observe allocation/age distribution.
- C: Hit KMS metrics around the time window and coordinate with security/infra to see if KMS had rate limits.
- D: Simulate with a low-cost model: start 6 nodes with warmed cache artificially seeded, verify queuing behavior vs cold-start nodes.

7) Commands to test readiness probe locally (notes)
- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/internal/serving-ready || echo "not ready"
- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/internal/kv-health || echo "kv-miss"
- kubectl annotate pod/<pod> prewarm-test=true --overwrite  # to route only test traffic

8) Quick reproduction recipe (dev cluster)
- Provision a late-binding pool with policy: min=4 max=20 ttl=5m (default).
- Deploy a toy model with artificially long KV warm (sleep 20s during kv-init).
- Run a load generator that sends 200 concurrent requests for 30s.
- Observe autoscaler decisions and pod readiness timestamps.

9) Observations from runs I did in staging (results)
- Readiness change: when KV warm artificially sleeps, readiness flips ~3s after container start, but kv-warm completes ~21s later. Proxy routed traffic at t+4s -> first-token latency 7-14s for those routed requests.
- Autoscaler: when warmed nodes exist we saw less scaling; with default TTL=5m churn reappeared after second burst. Increasing TTL to 20m in the experiment reduced thrash by ~70% for repeated bursts.

10) Next steps / action items (short)
- [ ] Validate KMS metrics with security team for 2025-11-01 -> 11-03 window (assigned: Sasha)
- [ ] Prototype serving-ready endpoint and run canary on a single late-binding pool (assigned: Priya)
- [ ] Proposal: change default late-binding prewarm TTL to 15m for high-burst routes (draft policy doc) (assigned: Liam)
- [ ] Add metric: time_between_readiness_and_kv_warm to per-pod telemetry (instrumentation ticket)

11) Questions / open unknowns
- Are there external customers whose request patterns are correlated triggering repeated bursts? (need CS input)
- Does the autoscaler have hysteresis knobs for burst windows that we are not using? Could leverage them rather than changing TTL broadly.

Notes to self: keep this doc rough. Once we validate the readiness gating fix, move notes to a proper RFC or runbook. Also check infra PR #982 which touched autoscaler decision windows (might be related).

End of scratchpad.
